implementation_notes: Kotlin gives null-safe interfaces, `sealed` hierarchies for closed extension, and `by` delegation which is the idiomatic substitute for the decorator/strategy object graphs SOLID tends to spawn. Inject dependencies through the primary constructor with `private val`, and use `internal` visibility so the implementation is not part of the published surface.
pitfalls: Platform types from Java interop silently weaken LSP checks at the boundary.
Extension functions used to add behaviour avoid touching the class but can scatter one responsibility across many files.
`sealed` hierarchies and open classes are a deliberate trade: sealing protects LSP but removes the extension point.
